title: [Bug]: Can't save global credentials in external storage
body:
### ⚠️ This issue respects the following points: ⚠️

- [x] This is a **bug**, not a question or a configuration/webserver/proxy issue.
- [x] This issue is **not** already reported on [Github](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Abug) OR [Nextcloud Community Forum](https://<redacted-host>/) _(I've searched it)_.
- [x] Nextcloud Server **is** up to date. See [Maintenance and Release Schedule](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/wiki/Maintenance-and-Release-Schedule) for supported versions.
- [x] I agree to follow Nextcloud's [Code of Conduct](https://nextcloud.com/contribute/code-of-conduct/).

### Bug description

Hi, 
A couple of weeks ago, there was a bug in Global Credentials ( https://github.com/nextcloud/server/issues/49349 ).
The temporary solution provided by @participant22 was working.
Now, after updating to Nextcloud 30.0.3 and 30.0.4, the Global Credentials can't be saved anymore.

The problem seems a bit different : when i input a new password, there is a input box, that ask for users's password to confirm the new password store in global credentials.
I tested and I checked my password : I'm sure it is the good one (the password is that is store in our OpenLDAP server).
Nextcloud says that the input password is wrong.




### Steps to reproduce

1. Log in to Nextcloud
2. Go to your Personnal parameters
3. Input a new password in Global Credentials aera
4. Save
5. Input your password to confirm


### Expected behavior

The input box that check your password, should verify your password.

### Nextcloud Server version

30

### Operating system

Debian/Ubuntu

### PHP engine version

PHP 8.2

### Web server

Apache (supported)

### Database engine version

MariaDB

### Is this bug present after an update or on a fresh install?

Updated from a MINOR version (ex. 28.0.1 to 28.0.2)

### Are you using the Nextcloud Server Encryption module?

Encryption is Disabled

### What user-backends are you using?

- [ ] Default user-backend _(database)_
- [x] LDAP/ Active Directory
- [ ] SSO - SAML
- [ ] Other

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
> @participant13 Does your commit https://github.com/nextcloud/server/commit/7c73c5c0586965317791ecfb51ac6769480cabd7 fix our problem ? (if yes, thanks in advance :-)

@participant12 yes, but it fixes a regression, depending on your version, it might not be why that was not working for you.


 
> Interesting... we have the same issue using php-fpm behind nginx. Any nginx modules we should be aware of?

Not sure, but you need to make sure your config allows Authorization headers.
For apache, this is set by our default htaccess IF you have `mod_env` enabled (which you should anyway when using Nextcloud)
For nginx, it could be worth investigating, especially if you use a reverse proxy.

comments.author: participant15
comments.body:
> Not sure, but you need to make sure your config allows Authorization headers. For apache, this is set by our default htaccess IF you have `mod_env` enabled (which you should anyway when using Nextcloud) For nginx, it could be worth investigating, especially if you use a reverse proxy.

That's probably a different issue, in our case if the wrong password is used for confirmation, the operation is rejected. The problem is different: per-share user credentials are modifiable, but Global Credentials for individual users are untouchable - in the past, it was possible to store them though. 
Maybe  I misunderstood the concept of Global Credentials, but it looks like per-user settings: one username and password which can be saved and applied for authentication to many shares. Is that right?

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
> That's probably a different issue, in our case if the wrong password is used for confirmation, the operation is rejected

if it gets rejected with a 401, it's exactly the issue.
Storing credentials have been updated to a more secure level and require the user password confirmation. Which fails as the password never gets asked.
You also need the mod_env to properly send the Auth. I fixed it here last week: https://github.com/nextcloud/server/pull/50910
